s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic painful intertriginous wounds with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques
Granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate with well-formed, nonnecrotizing granulomas
key_facts: 1.5-year history of painful intertriginous wounds
History of hypertension and depression
Multiple hospital admissions for cellulitis around the wounds
Received diverting sigmoid colostomy and indwelling urinary catheter
Wound care required nursing home care
Received adalimumab for 3 months without clinical improvement
Family history of similar condition
Linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques present in intertriginous areas
Histopathology showed pseudoepitheliomatous epidermal hyperplasia and granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate
Laboratory tests, including histochemical stains and tissue cultures, were negative
Elevated immunoglobulin G antibodies and flagellins

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated immunoglobulin G antibodies and flagellins, granulomatous inflammation, and family history of similar condition

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic painful intertriginous wounds with pseudoepitheliomatous epidermal hyperplasia and granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate

shortlist.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
shortlist.why_kept: Linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques present in intertriginous areas

shortlist.label: Granuloma inguinale
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of Langhans-type multinucleated giant cells

shortlist.label: Blau syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar condition and granulomatous inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of painful intertriginous wounds with linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques, and a history of multiple hospital admissions for cellulitis around the wounds, along with the histopathology showing pseudoepitheliomatous epidermal hyperplasia and granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate, is most consistent with Pyoderma gangrenosum. The lack of response to adalimumab and the presence of a family history of a similar condition also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: The patient's imaging studies, including computed tomography enterography, upper endoscopy, and colonoscopy, were unremarkable, making Crohn's disease less likely.

rejected.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
rejected.why: While the patient's presentation involves intertriginous areas, the presence of linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques and granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate on histopathology is more characteristic of Pyoderma gangrenosum.

rejected.label: Granuloma inguinale
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory tests, including histochemical stains and tissue cultures, were negative, making an infectious cause like Granuloma inguinale less likely.

rejected.label: Blau syndrome
rejected.why: While Blau syndrome can present with granulomatous dermatitis, the patient's age of onset and lack of other characteristic features, such as arthritis and uveitis, make this diagnosis less likely.
